title: SpaceX Plans a $74B AI Supercomputer Buildout, a Global Microsoft Outage Hits 130,000 Users, and Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO Ahead of Congressional Testimony
subhead: SpaceX maps out more than $74 billion for AI supercomputing campuses in Texas and Arizona as Nebius plans a $40 billion expansion; a global Microsoft 365 outage disrupts Outlook, Teams, and Intune; Nvidia names CFO Colette Kress interim CEO after Jensen Huang steps down; and the DOJ targets $1.2 billion in North Korean crypto loot.

sections.heading: SpaceX Plans $74B AI Supercomputer Buildout as Nebius Targets $40B and Cerebras Lands Microsoft Deal
sections.body:
SpaceX is planning to invest more than $74 billion across two massive AI supercomputer facilities—allocating over $24 billion to its Starbase complex in Texas and roughly $50 billion to a proposed campus in Arizona awaiting local regulatory approval—Bloomberg HT reported. Simultaneously, AI cloud challenger Nebius outlined plans to spend $40 billion on AI data center expansion funded through customer prepayments and debt, TechCrunch reported, while wafer-scale chipmaker Cerebras Systems saw its stock surge 17% after beating quarterly revenue estimates and announcing a new cloud compute partnership with Microsoft alongside existing deals with Amazon and Oracle, CNBC noted.

In academic hardware research, scientists at Brown University demonstrated a breakthrough in magnetic skyrmion control that could drastically cut the power consumption of future AI processors, Science Daily reported.
sections.whyItMatters: SpaceX's $74 billion supercomputer plan and Microsoft's deal with Cerebras show hyperscalers and aerospace giants building out massive compute capacity and alternative silicon stacks.

sections.heading: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO and Joins Commerce Secretary Lutnick on Congressional Witness List
sections.body:
Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang officially resigned as CEO on Thursday following reports of a third workplace relationship—reported by Reuters and TechCrunch—on top of an FBI counterintelligence probe into his affair with suspected Chinese intelligence intermediary Alice Huang, BBC, The Wall Street Journal, and Le Monde reported. Nvidia appointed chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO and Harvey Jones as board chair, Financial Times noted, even as more than 1,600 employees commented on an internal petition urging the board to reinstate Huang, according to Wired.

Both Huang and US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick agreed to testify before the Senate Banking and House Foreign Affairs committees after congressional Democrats opened a formal investigation into Huang's export dealings with the Trump administration and critics accused Lutnick of failing to stop the diversion of sensitive Nvidia AI chips to China, NBC News, CBS News, and The New York Times reported.
sections.whyItMatters: Dual congressional hearings featuring both Nvidia's ousted founder and the sitting Commerce Secretary virtually guarantee tighter US export licensing on AI semiconductors to China.

sections.heading: Global Microsoft 365 Outage Disrupts Outlook, Teams, and Intune for Over 130,000 Users
sections.body:
A severe global cloud outage disrupted Microsoft 365, Outlook, Teams, and Intune for more than five hours on Thursday, with nearly 130,000 users reporting access failures before recovery began, BBC, The Guardian, and The Register reported. Microsoft stated that a subset of backend servers unexpectedly became unavailable, cascading load onto remaining infrastructure, and acknowledged during the incident that initial remediation steps "have not provided the anticipated relief."

In defense space communications, Ukrainian officials told Ars Technica and The War Zone that SpaceX's Starshield military satellite network experienced renewed speed restrictions during Russian strikes—an allegation SpaceX denied—while Chinese AI satellite manufacturer Adaspace slipped in its Hong Kong stock market debut, CNA reported.
sections.whyItMatters: A multi-hour failure across Outlook, Teams, and Intune highlights enterprise single-point-of-failure risks in centralized productivity clouds.

sections.heading: Google Rolls Out Gemini 4 Hydrogen as FAA Expands AI Air Traffic Control Across US Airspace
sections.body:
Google rolled out its Gemini 4 Hydrogen model across Search AI Mode and developer APIs to replace Gemini 3.8 Flash, opting for an immediate global deployment rather than the phased safety rollouts used for its heavier Carbon and Argon models, Ars Technica and TechCrunch reported. At the same time, parent groups demanded moratoriums on Google AI tools on school-issued Chromebooks following a teen suicide lawsuit, while Google unveiled new camera-equipped smart glasses featuring mandatory recording indicator lights, The Register noted.

In public infrastructure, the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) expanded an AI advisory system to manage air traffic congestion across the entire US national airspace—winning praise from airlines despite complaints from the air traffic controllers' union that it was excluded from the rollout, Ars Technica reported. Meanwhile, European Union leaders prepared to hold their first dedicated summit talks on AI governance in Dublin, AFP reported, and developers released an uncensored Western fine-tune of Alibaba's Qwen 3.8 open-weight model, according to The Register.
sections.whyItMatters: Deploying AI traffic-management tools across the entire US airspace while families sue to pull generative AI from school Chromebooks illustrates the widening split between industrial and consumer AI adoption.

sections.heading: DOJ Targets $1.2B in Binance Crypto Loot as FBI Disrupts North Korean 'FaceStealer' Scam
sections.body:
The US Department of Justice (DOJ) moved to seize $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency routed through Binance as the FBI disrupted a North Korean state-linked cyber operation dubbed FaceStealer, which stole more than $400 million and recorded over 900 webcam sessions fromremote IT infiltration victims, The Register reported.

In commercial cybersecurity, OpenAI launched a suite of enterprise security products just as a coalition of nonprofits filed suit against major AI labs over AI-enabled cyberattacks, while Lego marketplace BrickLink remained offline for nearly a week following "unusual activity," The Register reported. In Turkey, Bankalararası Kart Merkezi (BKM) General Manager Ozan Deniz announced that domestic payment network Troy now processes one out of every four card transactions nationwide, while Samsung Turkey projected domestic smartphone sales will reach 12.5 million units this year, Dünya Gazetesi and Bloomberg HT reported.
sections.whyItMatters: The DOJ's $1.2 billion seizure action against North Korean crypto laundering shows how Pyongyang's remote-worker and deepfake schemes have scaled into billion-dollar state revenue streams.

bottomLine: Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia and forthcoming congressional testimony with Commerce Secretary Lutnick mark a watershed moment for US chip governance, even as SpaceX's $74 billion AI supercomputer plan and Nebius's $40 billion buildout accelerate global compute spending.
